name: How do you avoid a guest house feeling too close to neighbors?

mainEntity.name: What can be done when a backyard guest house is near the rear or side property line?
mainEntity.text: What can be done when a backyard guest house is near the rear or side property line?

acceptedAnswer.text: Proximity to neighbors is one of the most sensitive parts of a backyard build. A good design avoids direct window-to-window exposure, controls roof height, and uses landscaping or screened walls to soften the visual impact. Outdoor spaces should also be placed so they do not force constant sightlines into adjacent yards. In tight urban neighborhoods, the difference between a project that feels respectful and one that feels intrusive is often in the details. The best approach is to plan for privacy from the first sketch, not as an afterthought once the structure is already defined.
acceptedAnswer.description: When a guest house sits close to neighboring homes, privacy strategies become essential. Window placement, setback-aware massing, screening, landscaping, and careful outdoor lighting can reduce the feeling of crowding and improve comfort for everyone.
